headline: The NATIVE Act directs federal tourism and cultural agencies to include tribes and Native Hawaiian organizations in tourism planning, technical help, and cultural promotion.
what_it_does: The law requires the Commerce and Interior Departments and other agencies with travel or tourism roles to update their plans so they include tribes, tribal organizations, and Native Hawaiian organizations. Those plans must cover better tourism data, easier-to-use federal websites, tourism infrastructure support, bilingual signs, and transportation access. Interior and Commerce must also offer technical help to these groups on joining the tourism industry and report on that work. Federal agencies must support Native cultural showcasing, and grants for tourism, recreation, or travel may be used for cultural and arts projects, and the Smithsonian must share collections and do joint research with Native groups.

who_it_affects.group: Federally recognized Indian tribes and tribal organizations
who_it_affects.how: They may get technical help and grant funding to build tourism businesses and share their history and culture with visitors.
They are included in the same tourism planning, technical assistance, and grant eligibility as tribes.

who_it_affects.group: Travelers visiting tribal lands and federal recreation sites
who_it_affects.how: Agencies must plan for better visitor information, bilingual signage, and more respectful cultural experiences.

who_it_affects.group: Staff at the Commerce and Interior Departments and other federal travel agencies
who_it_affects.how: They must update management plans, provide technical assistance, and report on these efforts.

who_it_affects.group: Museums and cultural organizations working with the Smithsonian
who_it_affects.how: They may share collections and take part in joint research and projects with Native communities.
